title: 1994 AHSME Problem 2
statement:
A large rectangle is partitioned into four rectangles by two segments parallel to its sides. The areas of three of the resulting rectangles are shown. What is the area of the fourth rectangle?

 \(6\) \(14\)

 ? \(35\)

solutions.text: Let the column widths be \(u,v\) and the row heights be \(s,t.\) The displayed areas give \(us=6,\) \(vs=14,\) and \(vt=35.\) Therefore the missing area is \[ ut=\frac{(us)(vt)}{vs}=\frac{6\cdot35}{14}=15. \] Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Represent the two column widths and two row heights by variables
Products of diagonally opposite areas are equal
